## Failures

### `the_policy_stayed_inside_the_tire_model`

the deployed policy's worst slip angle reached 15.7 deg against our 12 deg bound, with 7.9% of steps beyond it (sampled, for comparison: 22.9 deg, 3.1% of steps — training-time only). Every minimum-time solve in Seasons 1 and 2 constrains this; the environment deliberately does not, so the policy is free to operate where the Magic Formula is extrapolating and the forces are arithmetic rather than measurement.

### `the_tire_file_s_own_load_range_was_respected`

7.9% of the deployed policy's steps left the tire file's own declared operating range (sampled: 3.1%). That bound is the file's, not ours, and outside it the model is not extrapolating from a fit — it has no fit.

## Technical notes

*Recorded, never pass/fail. These are where the model is correct but a reference is not, or where a number is worth watching.*

### the_two_action_dimensions_need_different_exploration

Steering rate and throttle have useful scales an order of magnitude apart — 0.037 of authority against the whole [-1, 1] interval — so a single exploration standard deviation cannot serve both. With one value small enough for the steering, the policy never sampled braking at all and sat at full throttle for half a million steps. This run uses [0.082, 0.368].
